subject: Physics
description: Newton's three laws of motion — inertia, F=ma, action-reaction; momentum, impulse, conservation, real-world applications.

questions.stem: Newton's FIRST LAW of motion is also known as the law of:

options.option_text: Inertia (objects at rest stay at rest)

questions.explanation: NEWTON'S FIRST LAW (Law of Inertia, 1687): 'A body at REST stays at REST, and a body in MOTION stays in MOTION at constant velocity, UNLESS acted upon by a NET EXTERNAL FORCE.' INERTIA = the tendency of an object to RESIST CHANGES in its state of motion. PROPORTIONAL TO MASS — heavier objects have MORE inertia. PRACTICAL EXAMPLES: (1) Sudden BUS BRAKING — passenger lurches FORWARD (their body wants to continue moving). (2) Sudden BUS ACCELERATION — passenger jerks BACKWARD. (3) Rotating tyres carry water/mud outward — tangential velocity. (4) When an apple is snapped from a tree, it falls — but earth pulls it down via gravity (a force). ALL THREE LAWS: (1) Inertia (1st). (2) F=ma (2nd). (3) Action-Reaction (3rd). HISTORICAL: pre-Galileo and Newton, ARISTOTLE believed objects need a continuous force to keep moving (incorrect). Galileo's ramp experiments showed objects in absence of friction would move forever — leading to the principle of inertia. Newton formalized it in PRINCIPIA MATHEMATICA (1687). PYQ FREQUENCY: Newton's laws are 1-mark guarantees in NEET, JEE-Main, NCERT-driven SSC, RRB.

questions.stem: Newton's SECOND LAW: F = ma. If a 5 kg mass accelerates at 2 m/s², the net force is:
questions.explanation: NEWTON'S SECOND LAW: F = m × a, where F = net force (newtons, N), m = mass (kg), a = acceleration (m/s²). Plug: F = 5 × 2 = 10 N. UNIT — NEWTON: 1 N = 1 kg·m/s² (force needed to accelerate 1 kg at 1 m/s²). EVERYDAY SCALE: an APPLE has weight ~1 N (mass ~100 g, g=10); a person of 70 kg weighs ~700 N. ALTERNATIVE FORMULATION: F = dp/dt — net force = rate of change of MOMENTUM (this form is more general; works for variable-mass systems like rockets). RELATED CONCEPT: WEIGHT W = mg (force due to gravity); on Earth W = m × 9.8 N; on Moon W = m × 1.6 N. INSIGHT: gravitation pulls everything towards Earth's center; Newton derived gravity AND motion laws from observation of falling apple + Moon's orbit. EVEN MORE GENERAL: in special relativity, F = dp/dt with relativistic momentum p = γmv (γ → ∞ as v → c). PYQ FREQUENCY: simple F=ma calculations appear 2-3× per JEE-Main, NEET; 1× per SSC CGL Tier 2.

questions.stem: Newton's THIRD LAW states 'For every action, there is an EQUAL and OPPOSITE reaction.' This explains:

options.option_text: Why a moving body slows down

questions.explanation: NEWTON'S THIRD LAW: 'F_AB = −F_BA' — when body A exerts a force on body B, body B simultaneously exerts an EQUAL but OPPOSITE force on A. ROCKET PROPULSION: hot gases pushed BACKWARD (action) → rocket pushed FORWARD (reaction). ALL of space-flight depends on this. WALKING: foot pushes ground BACKWARD (action) → ground pushes foot FORWARD (reaction); friction provides the necessary grip. SWIMMING: hands push water BACKWARD; water pushes swimmer FORWARD. JUMPING: legs push ground DOWN; ground pushes person UP. KEY MISCONCEPTIONS: (1) Action-reaction pair always acts on DIFFERENT BODIES (NOT the same body). (2) The pair has SAME MAGNITUDE but the EFFECTS may differ if masses are different — Earth and apple: same force, but Earth's mass is 10²⁵ × bigger, so Earth's acceleration is negligible. (3) Pair acts SIMULTANEOUSLY (no time delay). FAMOUS EXAMPLE: WERNHER VON BRAUN (rocket scientist) said Newton's 3rd law is 'all rocketry'. Saturn V (Apollo 11) generated 35 million N of thrust — by ejecting kerosene+oxygen at ~2,500 m/s. PYQ FREQUENCY: 3rd law applications are top NEET, JEE-Main, NCERT MCQ — 1-2× per cycle.

questions.explanation: MOMENTUM (linear momentum, p) = m × v, where m = mass (kg), v = velocity (m/s). UNITS: kg·m/s (or N·s, equivalent). VECTOR QUANTITY — has direction. CONSERVATION OF MOMENTUM: in an isolated system (no external force), TOTAL momentum is conserved. p_initial = p_final. APPLICATIONS: (1) COLLISIONS — billiard balls, car crashes: total momentum before = after. (2) ROCKET PROPULSION: rocket gains forward momentum equal to backward momentum of expelled gases. (3) RECOIL: when a gun fires, bullet gains momentum forward; gun gains equal momentum backward (recoil). NEWTON'S 2ND LAW REFORMULATED: F = dp/dt — force is the rate of change of momentum. So if you DOUBLE the time over which a force acts, you can HALVE the force needed for the same momentum change. EXAMPLE — AIRBAGS: increase impact TIME → reduce average force on driver → less injury. CRUMPLE ZONES in cars: same principle. CRICKET — when a player CATCHES a ball, they pull their hands BACK to extend the stopping time, reducing impact force on hand. PYQ FREQUENCY: momentum definition + conservation in NEET, JEE-Main 2-3× per paper; SSC CGL ~1× per cycle.

questions.stem: A bullet of mass 10 g is fired with velocity 400 m/s from a gun of mass 4 kg. The recoil velocity of the gun is:
questions.explanation: Apply CONSERVATION OF MOMENTUM. Before firing, gun + bullet are at REST → total momentum = 0. After firing, the bullet's forward momentum + gun's backward momentum = 0. Bullet momentum = (10/1000) × 400 = 4 kg·m/s (forward). Gun momentum = 4 × v (backward) = −4v kg·m/s. Setting sum = 0: 4 + (−4v) = 0 → 4v = 4 → v = 1 m/s. So the gun recoils at 1 m/s (much slower than bullet because gun's mass is 400× larger). KEY INSIGHT: (m_bullet × v_bullet) = (m_gun × v_recoil). RECOIL VELOCITY = (m_bullet/m_gun) × v_bullet. SAFETY: military rifles + sporting rifles use heavier stocks, recoil pads, gas-operated mechanisms to reduce recoil to manageable levels. SUMO/CANNON CONTRAST: cannons have wheeled carriages that move backward several meters when fired (e.g., 18th-century naval cannons recoiled 4-5m). KEY METHOD for momentum conservation: (1) identify SYSTEM. (2) write total p_before = total p_after. (3) solve for unknown. PYQ FREQUENCY: gun-recoil + 1D collision Qs in JEE-Main, NEET, SSC CGL Tier 2 — 1-2× per paper.

questions.explanation: IMPULSE (J) = F × Δt = CHANGE IN MOMENTUM (Δp). UNITS: N·s (or kg·m/s, same as momentum). VECTOR QUANTITY. KEY EQUATION: IMPULSE = J = ∫F·dt = Δp = m × Δv. APPLICATIONS: (1) AIRBAGS, CRUMPLE ZONES — same Δp, but extended Δt → reduced average F. (2) BOXING — punch lasts brief time → high force; defender 'rolls with the punch' → extends contact time → reduces force. (3) TRAMPOLINE — extends fall-stopping time, reducing force on body. (4) CATCHING A BALL — pulling hand back = longer contact = less impact. NUMERICAL EXAMPLE: car of mass 1000 kg moving at 20 m/s comes to rest in 5 s. Δp = 1000 × 20 = 20,000 kg·m/s. Average force = Δp/Δt = 20,000/5 = 4,000 N. If instead car stopped in 0.1 s (no crumple zone), Force = 20,000/0.1 = 200,000 N — 50× more dangerous. CONTRAST WITH WORK: work = F × distance (kJ); impulse = F × time (N·s). Work changes KE; impulse changes p. PYQ FREQUENCY: impulse-momentum theorem in JEE-Main, NEET 2× per cycle; SSC ~1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Two bodies of masses 2 kg and 3 kg moving with velocities 4 m/s and 2 m/s respectively (in opposite directions) collide and stick together. The final velocity is:
questions.explanation: PERFECTLY INELASTIC COLLISION (objects stick together post-collision). Apply CONSERVATION OF MOMENTUM. Take direction of 2 kg's velocity as positive. Before: p_total = (2)(4) + (3)(−2) = 8 − 6 = +2 kg·m/s. After: total mass = 2+3 = 5 kg; final velocity v_f. So 5v_f = 2 → v_f = 0.4 m/s in the original direction of the 2-kg body (positive). KEY: KE is NOT conserved in inelastic collisions — some energy converts to heat, deformation, sound. LET'S CHECK: KE_before = ½(2)(16) + ½(3)(4) = 16 + 6 = 22 J. KE_after = ½(5)(0.16) = 0.4 J. KE LOST = 21.6 J — significant! That's the deformation energy. TYPES of COLLISIONS: (1) ELASTIC — both p and KE conserved (e.g., billiard balls, atoms). (2) INELASTIC — only p conserved; some KE lost. (3) PERFECTLY INELASTIC — bodies stick; max KE loss for given p. REAL CARS: collisions are ~80-95% inelastic; explains why KE lost goes into deforming metal/airbags. PYQ FREQUENCY: 1D collision problems in JEE-Main 2-3× per paper, NEET 1-2× per cycle. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests momentum conservation discipline + sign convention.
